## REQ-LIFE-001

**Birth message on every connection**

A component publishes a Birth message whenever its connection to the broker is established, i.e. after every connect and every reconnect.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.3, SF-059
- Verification: d7-monitor, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.3.3-7027f33a

> This message must be published whenever the connection between client and broker is established.
> — MG 6.3.3

> The protocol version, the broker address and ports, the security settings as well as the birth message and the will message are mandatory for all levels.
> — MG 6

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-003. The Birth message should be the first message after the connection is established (REQ-LIFE-015). D7 checks it by forcing a reconnect of the application under test (test broker).

## REQ-LIFE-002

**Birth message topic**

The Birth message is published to the topic Oi4v2/&lt;ServiceType>/&lt;AppId>/Pub/MAM/&lt;AppId>, i.e. the Source is the AppId of the component itself.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.3, MG 7.6
- Verification: d7-monitor
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.3.3-55175294

> It must be published to the topic Oi4v2/&lt;ServiceType>/&lt;AppId>/Pub/MAM/&lt;AppId>, i.e. the Source is the AppId of the application itself (7.6 Source Element).
> — MG 6.3.3

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-003. The topic syntax is area TOP.

## REQ-LIFE-003

**Birth message is the MAM of the component itself**

The Birth message is a complete Pub MAM NetworkMessage (MG 8.1) with one DataSetMessage of type MAM whose Payload is the Master Asset Model of the component itself (ProductInstanceUri is the component's own Identification Link). It is identical in content to the component's regular Pub MAM about itself and uses the same DataSetWriterId.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 5, MG 6, MG 6.3.3, MG 8.1, SF-057
- Verification: d7-validate, d7-monitor
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.3.3-3ac518a8, MG-6.3.3-bee211aa

> In an Open Industry 4.0 Alliance context, the Birth message must contain a NetworkMessage with a DataSetMessage of type Master Asset Model (5 The Master Asset Model) of the application.
> — MG 6.3.3

> It must refer to the topic resource MAM (7.5.1 Resources) and share its payload.
> — MG 6.3.3

Notes: Keywords added in C-026 (SF-057 (f)). The envelope rules of a Pub message apply (area MSG); the Birth message is a regular Pub MAM, so ReplyTo is empty and the MessageId carries the time of the publication (MG 8.2.1, SF-058 (a)). Example: V-PAY-023. Reclassified in C-035 (+d7-validate, Q-020 (a), ADR-0019 §9): with a declared role birth (vector field role, D7 validate --role) the single-message part is checked offline – a Pub MAM with exactly one DataSetMessage whose ProductInstanceUri is the AppId. The same DataSetWriterId as the regular Pub MAM stays with d7-monitor. Reclassified in C-041 (-schema, consistency review of the P2 exit, ADR-0019 §9): the role of a Birth message is not visible in one message, so no entry schema can check it; the schema checks the message as a regular Pub MAM under the MAM and MSG requirements. The single-message part with a declared role is the rule layer's (R-6, D7 validate --role).

## REQ-LIFE-004

**Birth message without Timestamp and SequenceNumber**

The DataSetMessage of the Birth message does not contain the optional keys Timestamp and SequenceNumber.

- Keyword: SHOULD NOT
- Levels: L1 SHOULD NOT · L2 SHOULD NOT · L3 SHOULD NOT
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6.3.3, MG 8.2.3, SF-058, SF-061
- Verification: d7-monitor
- Status: deprecated

Notes: Withdrawn by the PO (review of C-026, SF-061 (a)): "the content of this keys can not be pre-set" holds for the Will message registered at the broker, not for the Birth message the application publishes itself. The Birth message is a regular MAM message; Timestamp and SequenceNumber may be used like in any other MAM message (MG 6.3.3 note, MG-6.3.3-61f18ab8 in coverage/informative.yaml). The id is not reused.

## REQ-LIFE-005

**Close message before a graceful disconnect**

A component publishes a Close message before it closes its connection to the broker gracefully.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.4, SF-061
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-eafd1d73, MG-6.3.4-1e141d2f

> An application-driven message must be published in OI4 Alliance context before the connection is closed gracefully.
> — MG 6.3.4

> The close message is recommended for Level 1 and mandatory from Level 2 on.
> — MG 6

Notes: PO review of C-026 (SF-061 (b)): must from Level 2 on (was should at all levels). Graded by REQ-CMP-046. A graceful disconnect discards the Will message at the broker; without a Close message other participants are not informed. D7 needs the application under test to be stopped gracefully.

## REQ-LIFE-007

**Close message content**

The Close message is a Pub Health NetworkMessage (MG 8.1) with one DataSetMessage of type Health whose Payload is Health NORMAL_0 and HealthScore 0. It uses the DataSetWriterId of the component's Health about itself.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Condition: The component publishes a Close message (REQ-LIFE-005).
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.4, MG 8.3.2, SF-057, SF-058
- Verification: d7-validate, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-eafd1d73, MG-6.3.4-3ff69c8d, MG-6.3.4-58771e2c

> The Close message must contain the health information for a graceful disconnect of the application (8.3.2 Health).
> — MG 6.3.4

> It must refer to the topic resource Health (7.5.1 Resources) and share its payload.
> — MG 6.3.4

Notes: Keywords added in C-026 (SF-057 (g)); the payload values are given by the code block of MG 6.3.4. Graded by REQ-CMP-046 (SF-061 (b), C-026). The MessageId carries the time of the publication; Timestamp and SequenceNumber may be used like in any Health message (SF-058, B1.1.2). Example: V-PAY-024. Reclassified in C-035 (+d7-validate, Q-020 (a), ADR-0019 §9): with a declared role close (vector field role, D7 validate --role) the single-message part is checked offline – a Pub Health with exactly one DataSetMessage, Health NORMAL_0 and HealthScore 0. The DataSetWriterId of the regular Health stays with d7-test. Reclassified in C-041 (-schema, consistency review of the P2 exit, ADR-0019 §9): the role of a Close message is not visible in one message, so no entry schema can check it; the schema checks the message as a regular Pub Health under the Health and MSG requirements. The single-message part with a declared role is the rule layer's (R-6, D7 validate --role).

## REQ-LIFE-008

**Will message registered on every connection**

A component registers a Will message in every MQTT CONNECT, with the topic Oi4v2/&lt;ServiceType>/&lt;AppId>/Pub/Health/&lt;AppId> (the Source is the AppId of the component itself) and the Will Retain flag false.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.2, MG 6.3.5, MG 7.6, SF-057
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.3.5-ab380d71

> The Will message must be registered at the broker whenever the connection is established, with the topic Oi4v2/&lt;ServiceType>/&lt;AppId>/Pub/Health/&lt;AppId>, i.e. the Source is the AppId of the application itself (7.6 Source Element).
> — MG 6.3.5

> The protocol version, the broker address and ports, the security settings as well as the birth message and the will message are mandatory for all levels.
> — MG 6

Notes: Keyword added in C-026 (SF-057 (h)); the Will message is mandatory per the MG 6 note (REQ-CMP-003). Retain false follows from REQ-MQTT-018. D7 checks it by cutting the connection of the application under test (test broker).

## REQ-LIFE-009

**Will message content**

The Will message is a Pub Health NetworkMessage (MG 8.1) with one DataSetMessage of type Health whose Payload is Health FAILURE_1 and HealthScore 0. It uses the DataSetWriterId of the component's Health about itself: all Health messages the component publishes about itself (Source = AppId) after registering the Will message use the same DataSetWriterId as the Will message.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.5, MG 8.2.3, MG 8.3.2, SF-057
- Verification: d7-validate, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.3.5-38d4d8c4, MG-6.3.5-572831c0, MG-6.3.5-c27255e4

> The Will message must contain the predefined health information for an ungraceful disconnect of the application (8.3.2 Health).
> — MG 6.3.5

> It must refer to topic resource Health (7.5.1 Resources) and share its payload.
> — MG 6.3.5

> All Health messages that the application publishes about itself (Source = AppId) after registering the Will message must therefore use this DataSetWriterId as well.
> — MG 6.3.5

Notes: Keywords added in C-026 (SF-057 (h)). The DataSetWriterId binding to the later Health messages was made explicit in MG 6.3.5 on PO request (C-032 log addendum 43). The MessageId of the Will message is REQ-LIFE-016. Example: V-PAY-025. Reclassified in C-035 (+d7-validate, Q-020 (a), ADR-0019 §9): with a declared role will (vector field role, D7 validate --role) the single-message part is checked offline – a Pub Health with exactly one DataSetMessage, Health FAILURE_1 and HealthScore 0. The DataSetWriterId shared with the later Health messages stays with d7-test. Reclassified in C-041 (-schema, consistency review of the P2 exit, ADR-0019 §9): the role of a Will message is not visible in one message, so no entry schema can check it; the schema checks the message as a regular Pub Health under the Health and MSG requirements. The single-message part with a declared role is the rule layer's (R-6, D7 validate --role).

The DataSetMessage of the Will message does not contain the optional keys Timestamp and SequenceNumber.

## REQ-LIFE-011

**Subscribers interpret the Close message**

A subscriber that tracks the online state of applications (e.g. the Registry) interprets a Health message of an application about itself with Health NORMAL_0 and HealthScore 0 as Close message: the application went offline gracefully.

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: subscriber, registry
- Condition: The subscriber tracks the online state of other applications.
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.4, SF-059, SF-061
- Verification: manual, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-eafd1d73, MG-6.3.4-4de9c16e

> Subscribers that keep track of the online state of applications, such as the Registry, should interpret a Health message of an application about itself with Health NORMAL_0 and HealthScore 0 as Close message: the application went offline gracefully.
> — MG 6.3.4

Notes: Subscriber scope added in C-026 (SF-059 (b)); should at all levels (PO review of C-026, SF-061 (c): application logic). A message "about itself" is one with Source equal to the AppId of the publisher.

## REQ-LIFE-012

**Subscribers interpret the Will message**

A subscriber that tracks the online state of applications (e.g. the Registry) interprets a Health message of an application about itself with Health FAILURE_1 and HealthScore 0 as an ungraceful disconnect: the application is offline and not available anymore. This also holds if the application is still connected and published the message itself (e.g. a completely broken device).

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: subscriber, registry
- Condition: The subscriber tracks the online state of other applications.
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.5, SF-059, SF-061
- Verification: manual, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.3.5-22c19cbf, MG-6.3.5-820ce30c

> Subscribers that keep track of the online state of applications, such as the Registry, should interpret a Health message of an application about itself with Health FAILURE_1 and HealthScore 0 as an ungraceful disconnect: the application is offline and not available anymore.
> — MG 6.3.5

> An application that is still connected may also publish a Health message about itself with Health FAILURE_1 and HealthScore 0, e.g. a device that is completely broken; subscribers then consider it not available as well.
> — MG 6.3.5

Notes: Subscriber scope and the still connected case added in C-026 (SF-059 (a), (b)); should at all levels (PO review of C-026, SF-061 (c): application logic).

## REQ-LIFE-013

**Online again after the next Birth message**

A subscriber that tracks the online state of applications considers an application that went offline or not available (Close message, Will message or FAILURE_1/0 about itself) online again only after it received the application's next Birth message.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: subscriber, registry
- Condition: The subscriber tracks the online state of other applications.
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.3, MG 6.3.5, SF-057, SF-059
- Verification: manual, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.3.5-63c2640b

> These subscribers must consider the application online again only after its next Birth message (6.3.3 Birth Message).
> — MG 6.3.5

Notes: Keyword added in C-026 (SF-057 (i)).

## REQ-LIFE-014

**Close Health values are reserved**

A component does not publish a Health message about itself with Health NORMAL_0 and HealthScore 0 other than as its Close message (REQ-LIFE-007).

- Keyword: MUST NOT
- Levels: L1 SHOULD NOT · L2 MUST NOT · L3 MUST NOT
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.4, MG 8.3.2, SF-059
- Verification: d7-monitor
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-eafd1d73, MG-6.3.4-9e2665bf

> An application must not publish a Health message about itself with Health NORMAL_0 and HealthScore 0 other than as its Close message.
> — MG 6.3.4

Notes: Added in C-026 (SF-059 (a)); graded by REQ-CMP-046 (MG 6.3.4, SF-061 (b)). A Health about an asset (Source other than the AppId) is not affected. FAILURE_1 with HealthScore 0 is not reserved (REQ-LIFE-012, REQ-LIFE-017).

## REQ-LIFE-015

**Birth message first after connect**

The Birth message is the first message a component publishes after its connection to the broker is established.

## REQ-LIFE-016

**Will message MessageId carries its creation time**

A component creates its Will message anew for every connection; its MessageId carries the timestamp of its creation (MG 8.2.1), i.e. of the registration at connect time.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.5, MG 8.2.1, SF-058
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.3.5-8738574b

> The Will message is created anew for every connection: like in any other message, its MessageId must carry the timestamp of its creation (8.2.1 NetworkMessage).
> — MG 6.3.5

Notes: Added in C-026 (SF-058 (a), variant "current timestamp"). A client library that re-sends a registered Will unchanged on automatic reconnects does not fulfil it. Example: V-PAY-025.

## REQ-LIFE-017

**Birth message again after recovery**

A component that published a Health message about itself with Health FAILURE_1 and HealthScore 0 while still connected publishes its Birth message again when it is available again.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Condition: The component published FAILURE_1/0 about itself while connected.
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.3, MG 6.3.5, SF-059
- Verification: d7-test, manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.3.5-22c19cbf, MG-6.3.5-b8b20f8f

> When such an application is available again, it must publish its Birth message again (6.3.3 Birth Message).
> — MG 6.3.5

Notes: Added in C-026 (SF-059 (a)): FAILURE_1/0 is not reserved for the Will message; publishing it while connected is allowed (MAY, e.g. a completely broken device). Subscribers consider the component available again only after the Birth message (REQ-LIFE-013).
